target_customer: Patients with Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis, with research partners as potential payers
problem: Patients with chronic bowel disease had little shared data on which treatments and diets worked, and no easy way to contribute to research.
business_model: Free patient network; planned revenue from research collaborations and data partnerships
product_category: Patient symptom tracking and research network

founders.name: Sean Ahrens
education: University of California, Berkeley, computer science
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch (2012-08-20) says he was diagnosed with Crohn's at age 12; YC bio lists MessageParty, Crohnology, IBDPartners.

founders.name: Will Cole
education: University of California, Berkeley, computer science
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch says he and Ahrens studied computer science at Berkeley.

exit.reason: Ahrens has said in an interview that he could not raise funding; no formal shutdown notice found.

technical_complexity.rationale: A web symptom tracker and social network is standard engineering; the harder parts were patient privacy and data quality.

defensibility.rationale: Accumulated patient data and a community of about 27,000 to 30,000 members were hard to copy, but the data had to be monetized by partners.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: The CCFA later ran its own patient powered research network (press release 2018) on which Ahrens was a coauthor affiliated with Crohnology.

market_need_then: Ahrens, a Crohn's patient, started it from his own experience, and TechCrunch (2012-08-20) described it as a destination for people with chronic illness; the site later reached over 27,000 patients per the YC page.

branding.name_origin: Crohnology is a blend of Crohn's and the suffix for study, implied by the product, but no source states the origin.
branding.domain_note: Used crohnology.com; the domain stopped resolving around 2021 per a directory.

identity.voice_and_tone: Patient empowerment: tagline We turn Patients into Researchers.

branding.brand_signature: We turn Patients into Researchers tagline
branding.community_and_virality: Reached about 27,000 patients organically per the YC page and about 30,000 per Ahrens; Scientific American coverage and research partners including UNC and Genentech are listed by the YC page.

brand_strength.rationale: A clear niche identity with a strong tagline and research partner mentions, but narrow awareness and a name tied to one disease.

outcome_analysis: Crohnology was built by a Crohn's patient and a fellow Berkeley engineer, grew organically to roughly 27,000 patients and attracted research partners. Ahrens has said he could not raise the funding to continue and that the company was underfunded, and the site went offline around 2021. The disease specific market and research data business model were hard to fund, though no formal shutdown notice exists.
notes: crohnology.com returned HTTP 522 when fetched; a directory reports it has not resolved since 2021. The Rock Health seed (2011-11) rests on a single AI labeled Dealroom page with no amount. The 2012-08-01 row on Seedtable is the last funding date with no amount or investors and is probably the YC deal. One source adds Sarah Branon as a developer and Dealroom calls her a co-founder; the YC page and TechCrunch do not, so she is not listed. The Ahrens quote comes from a summary page, not a first hand interview that I opened. TechCrunch (2012-08-20) names no competitors, so the list is empty.
